references.text: Philip was from Bethsaida, the same town as Andrew and Peter. After being called by Jesus, Philip found Nathanael and told him about Jesus ([ref:Joh 1:44-45|John 1:44-45]).

Philip is mentioned again in conversation with Jesus, this time at the feeding of the five thousand, which shows the continued relationship between Jesus and Philip after his calling ([ref:Joh 6:5-7|John 6:5-7]).
Philip acts as a mediator when Greeks wish to meet Jesus, showing his role among the disciples after he followed Jesus' call ([ref:Joh 12:21-22|John 12:21-22]).

Philip asks Jesus to show them the Father, and Jesus responds by explaining His relationship with the Father. This shows Philip's continued walk with Jesus after his initial calling ([ref:Joh 14:8-9|John 14:8-9]).
Jesus calls Peter and Andrew with the words "Follow me" (Ἀκολουθεῖτέ μοι), the same call given to Philip here ([ref:Matt 4:19-20|Matthew 4:19-20]).
Jesus calls Matthew with the same word "Follow me" (Ἀκολούθει μοι), parallel to the calling of Philip ([ref:Matt 9:9|Matthew 9:9]).
Jesus' call to Levi with the words "Follow me" (Ἀκολούθει μοι) is identical to the call given to Philip ([ref:Mark 2:14|Mark 2:14]).
Luke's account of the calling of Levi with "Follow me" (Ἀκολούθει μοι) follows the same pattern as Jesus' call to Philip ([ref:Luk 5:27-28|Luke 5:27-28]).
Philip is listed among the twelve apostles, confirming that he was one of those Jesus called to follow Him ([ref:Matt 10:2-4|Matthew 10:2-4]).

The day before Philip's calling, Andrew and another disciple found Jesus and followed Him. This shows a pattern where Jesus gathers disciples around Himself, one after another ([ref:Joh 1:35-40|John 1:35-40]).
Elijah calls Elisha to follow him as a prophetic disciple by throwing his cloak over him, an Old Testament foreshadowing of Jesus' call to discipleship ([ref:1 Kong 19:19-21|1 Kings 19:19-21]).
